The verse of Tayammum came when Aisha's lost necklace held the people without water; the earth, the Prophet said, was made for his followers a place of prayer and Tayammum.
The Prophet did Tayammum on a wall to return a greeting, and taught Ammar, who had rolled in dust when Junub, that stroking earth and wiping face and hands suffices.
A Junub man without water was told Tayammum suffices, and a woman's water bags quenched all; Ibn Mas'ud refused it to the Junub, fearing its use when water was cold.
When Asma's necklace was lost and the men searching for it prayed without ablution for lack of water, Allah revealed the verse of tayammum.
When Aisha's necklace was lost and the people had no water, Abu Bakr rebuked her; then the verse of tayammum came and the necklace was found under her camel.
When a necklace Aisha borrowed was lost and searchers prayed without ablution, the verse of Tayammum was revealed, and Usaid bin Hudair praises the blessing she brought.
When a necklace Aisha had borrowed from Asma was lost, the men searching for it prayed without ablution for lack of water, and Allah revealed the verse of Tayammum.
